claims.claim: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in the final on 19 July 2026
claims.note: FIFA: final on July 19, 2026 (photo caption); Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 after extra time.

claims.claim: Spain's 2026 title was its second World Cup title, following its 2010 triumph
claims.note: FIFA: 'second FIFA World Cup title, following their triumph in 2010'.

claims.claim: Simón kept seven clean sheets, the most by any goalkeeper in a single World Cup edition
claims.note: FIFA and Fox Sports both say seven, the most by a goalkeeper in one edition.

claims.claim: Spain conceded one goal across eight matches
claims.note: FIFA: 'conceded just one goal across eight matches'.

claims.claim: Spain scored 14 goals, their highest World Cup tally
claims.note: FIFA: 'Their total of 14 goals represented their highest-ever tally'.

claims.claim: Simón was presented with the Golden Glove (FIFA photo caption) and was awarded it for the tournament
claims.note: FIFA caption 'Unai Simon #23 of Spain is presented with the Golden Glove'; Fox: 'has been awarded the 2026 FIFA World Cup Golden Glove'.

claims.claim: Simón was born on 11 June 1997 in Vitoria-Gasteiz
claims.note: LaLiga 11-06-1997 and Vitoria-Gasteiz; Wikidata 11 June 1997 and Vitoria-Gasteiz.

claims.claim: Wikidata records Spanish citizenship
claims.note: Wikidata country of citizenship: Spain.

claims.claim: LaLiga lists him as a goalkeeper (Portero) for Athletic Club, height 190 cm
claims.note: LaLiga profile: 190 cm, Athletic Club, Portero.

claims.claim: CD Aurrera had a partnership agreement with Athletic; coach Javier Barbero recruited him at eleven
claims.note: Vavel: partnership agreement with Athletic; Barbero recruited him at the age of eleven.

claims.claim: He worked his way up through Lezama after joining Athletic's youth system and the cadet side
claims.note: Vavel: joined the cadet side; worked his way up through Lezama.

claims.claim: CD Basconia was his first taste of senior football; promoted to Bilbao Athletic in summer 2016
claims.note: Vavel: 'first taste of senior football came at CD Basconia'; summer 2016 promotion to Bilbao Athletic.

claims.claim: La Liga debut on 20 August 2018 at San Mamés, a 2-1 win over Leganés, aged 21
claims.note: Vavel: debut 20 August 2018, 2-1 win over Leganés, at 21.

claims.claim: He has spent his whole professional career at Athletic Club
claims.note: Vavel: 'has spent his whole professional career at Athletic Club'.

claims.claim: In September 2024 Football España reported a contract extension at Athletic until 2029 after rejecting Saudi Pro League interest
claims.note: Football España: extension until 2029 after rejecting Saudi Pro League transfer interest.

claims.claim: He signed a new contract in May 2024
claims.note: Vavel: 'In May 2024 he signed a new contract, with no release clause.'

claims.claim: Quote: 'I want to be the world's best goal keeper here at Athletic Club.' Outlet expected him to finish his career at San Mamés
claims.note: Football España quote and 'expected to complete his career at the Estadio San Mames'.

claims.claim: Luis Enrique gave him his Spain debut on 11 November 2020, a 1-1 friendly against the Netherlands
claims.note: Vavel: debut 11 November 2020, 1-1 friendly against the Netherlands.

claims.claim: Club honours (2021 Super Cup, 2024 Copa del Rey, Zamora Trophy 2023-24) and Spain honours (2015 U19 Euro, 2019 U21 Euro, Tokyo silver, 2023 Nations League, Euro 2024)
claims.note: Vavel honours list matches all items.

claims.claim: He played through a persistent wrist injury at Euro 2024, had surgery afterwards and was not expected back until the start of 2025
claims.note: Football España: 'played through the pain at the tournament'; surgery on a persistent wrist injury; not expected back until start of 2025.

claims.claim: David Raya and Joan García, the Premier League and La Liga Golden Glove winners, were Spain's second and third goalkeepers
claims.note: Fox: 'who were waiting behind him as Spain's No. 2 and No. 3 goalkeepers, respectively.'

claims.claim: He credited Luis de la Fuente for choosing him to start
claims.note: Fox: 'Simón rewarded Luis de la Fuente for giving him the nod'.

claims.claim: Fox Sports describes his shot-stopping as reliable, says he came out to deal with balls over the top, and credits him with strong command of his box
claims.note: Fox: 'He was reliable with his shot-stopping'; 'came out to deal with balls over the top'; 'strong command of his box throughout the entire World Cup'.

claims.claim: He worked well with centre-backs Aymeric Laporte and Pau Cubarsí
claims.note: Fox: 'Aymeric Laporte and Pau Cubarsí helped form one of the best defensive units'.

claims.claim: Fox Sports reports seven clean sheets, breaking the record for a goalkeeper at a single World Cup
claims.note: Fox: 'breaking the record for the most clean sheets by a goalkeeper at a single World Cup'.

claims.claim: Entering the final Spain had conceded one goal; the 1-0 win was the fewest goals conceded by any champion
claims.note: Fox: 'Entering the final, Simón had conceded only one goal'; 'the fewest goals any team has ever conceded on the way to winning the tournament'.

claims.claim: The final was his fourth major international tournament; three clean sheets in six Euro matches
claims.note: Fox: 'Now playing in his fourth major international tournament'; 'keeping three clean sheets across six matches'.

claims.claim: Spain outshot Argentina 20-2; Simón said his hands did not have to work as hard as other keepers; 14 saves; record seventh World Cup shutout
claims.note: Asharq Al-Awsat: outshot 20-2; interpreter quote; needed only 14 saves; 'record seventh shutout'.

claims.claim: Spain's only goal conceded before the final came in a 2-1 quarter-final win over Belgium; the 2010 champions shared the record of two goals allowed
claims.note: Asharq Al-Awsat: only Belgium scored in a 2-1 quarter-final; 2010 team shared the previous record of two goals allowed.

claims.claim: Emiliano Martínez made a record 11 saves in the final
claims.note: Asharq Al-Awsat: 'finishing with a record 11'.

claims.claim: He is 29 as of 27 October 2026, born 11 June 1997
claims.note: Date of birth from LaLiga; arithmetic from the date of the check.

valueNote: Sets out the 2026 World Cup clean-sheet record with primary FIFA data, a dated timeline from Athletic's youth system to Spain, and the final's shot and save figures, which the usual top results do not give in one place.
summary: All claims checked against the opened sources after the fixes (fourth tier removed, shot-stopping reworded to Fox Sports wording, 2010 and 1-0 claim limited to what FIFA states, final date cited to FIFA). The translated sentences were checked against the same facts.
